That's a pretty novel idea. It wouldn't help people who already have Alzheimers, but it would be a pretty epic vaccine against it.

From what I recall from my genetics course (in which we talked about Alzh in some detail for whatever reason), the "in a nutshell" laymens explanation of why people develop Alzh (or at least one of the leading theories as to why) is that when your cells divide you have these long proteins sticking out of each cell which are then trimmed by enzymes. If you have a defective enzyme (or two or a million) the protein will be incorrectly cut resulting in a mis-fold that does not, biochemically, interact with any other part of your body in any significant way (including an incredible difficulty of actually getting rid of them from your body)*. These misfolded proteins are, however, "sticky" to each other and usually accumulate in bunches in the brain, causing plaques (along with aluminum ions...chicken or the egg?). I doubt that antibodies would be able to handle bunched up palques, but if you are at risk of developing Alzh then a vaccine for modified antibodies should, theoretically, stop these buildups before they even begin.

*There has been at least one recent study that has noted that when you sleep Cerebro Spinal Fluid (CSF) flushes into your brain to interact with the brain's InterStitial Fluid (ISF), through newly discovered vasculature, and helps, to a small extent, "flush out" plaques and beta amyloids (misfolded proteins). This could be another clue for why children need to sleep much longer than adults; their cells divide at a much more accelerated rate and beta amyloids are far more likely to happen due to volume, rate, and chance.
